metadata.case_name: MAK CHUN TO v. OCEAN PLASTIC FACTORY

plaintiff.occupation_before: Plastic moulding machine operator; also employed by Hong Kong United Dockyards

injuries.description: Amputation of all four fingers of the right hand to the wrist on the inner side.
source: Admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital where all 4 fingers of the right hand were amputated to the wrist on the inner side. No loss of consciousness, wound treated and stitched.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of two or more fingers at or near base, right hand

injuries.description: Transplant of the left second toe into the hand stump (transplant failed and was removed), with resulting scars on the left foot and sole.
source: Admitted to Caritas Hospital for a transplant of the left second toe into the hand stump. Five inch scar between big toe and 3rd toe, plus a 3?inch scar on the sole. Transplant failed to take and was removed one month later in stages over a period of 3 months.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of wrist or hand, unspecified

injuries.description: Second transplant to the right hand stump consisting of half of right big toe and part of the bones of the right second toe (transplant taken but of little use).
injuries.body_part: right foot (partial right big toe and part of right second toe)
source: Admitted to Prince of Wales Hospital for second transplant to the right hand stump of half of right big toe and part of the bones of the right second toe, followed by a small skin graft from the left thigh applied to the base of the transplanted toe. This transplant has taken but the plaintiff said in evidence that it was of no great use to him. From his demonstration in court I readily accept this. Dr. Mao's report confirmed that the toe was of little use.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at or near base of right thumb

injuries.description: Abdominal flap graft to provide fresh skin for the right hand stump with an eight inch linear scar on right flank.
source: Re-admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital for an abdominal flap graft to provide fresh skin for the right hand stump. Eight inch linear scar on right flank of body. Discharged for physiotherapy until 19th November 1984.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

injuries.description: Skin grafts from the left thigh for wound that refused to heal.
source: Wound refused to heal and re-admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital for skin grafts from the left thigh. Healed in June 1985.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of hip or thigh, unspecified

manifestations.description: Loss of feeling near the areas from which toes were removed and on large areas of the hand stump
Pain when the plaintiff walks for more than 45 minutes
Inability to play basketball, ride a cycle and drive
Transplanted toe was of little use as a substitute for a middle finger
Horrifying appearance of the injured hand causing cosmetic disfigurement and diminished marriage prospects

treatments_received: Amputation of four fingers of the right hand (10th-16th October 1983)
Physiotherapy (5 times weekly for 3 months and continued outpatient physiotherapy thereafter)
Transplant of left second toe into hand stump (February/November 1984) - transplant failed and removed
Second transplant (half of right big toe and part of right second toe) to right hand stump (September 1985)
Small skin graft from left thigh to base of transplanted toe

losses.description: Amputation of all four fingers of the right hand to the wrist causing loss of use of the hand
Horrifying appearance of injured hand and scars (including eight inch linear scar on right flank and scars on feet) leading to cosmetic disfigurement
Pain when walking for more than 45 minutes and inability to run

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Inability to play basketball, ride a cycle and drive
Diminished marriage prospects due to appearance and diminished economic status
